changelog.change: palette gains `art_panel`; polyhaven-hanging_picture_frame_01 gains the partial material_override {hanging_picture_frame_01_artwork -> art_panel} under an unchanged `keep_source` policy.
changelog.why: Found by eye on the T13 FINALS at 1:1: the frame's shipped artwork texture is a Poly Haven placeholder that reads 'Ray Hopes / Photo: 76cm x 51cm / Frame: 84cm x 59cm'. It was illegible while the frame hung with its centre at 192 cm and became legible the moment F-360-159 lowered it to eye level — the fix exposed the defect. Six rooms of a tour of a REAL apartment would have carried a framed third-party placard.
changelog.cost: ⚠ Not free: the style lock's sha256 is in `inputs.style_sha256` and build_scene.py's sha256 is in `generator.script_sha256`, both inside every point's render key — so this one material invalidates ALL TWELVE points, not the seven rooms that have art. Paid deliberately: a manifest whose keys match the scene is worth more than 5 saved renders, and a forged checkpoint is not an option.

changelog.change: lighting.pendant_bulb.energy_w: a bare 30.0 -> the string rule '40 + 6 * area_m2' — the SAME rule lighting.ceiling_luminaire already used. No new coefficient was invented.
changelog.why: The 12-point draft strip measured an INVERTED luminaire law: the seven small rooms that get a ceiling disk were area-scaled (52.5-100.3 W) and the four LARGEST rooms — living 15.89, dining 15.77, master 11.82, bed-2 9.08 m², the ones a buyer looks at longest — were the only ones NOT scaled, at a flat 30 W each. Measured mean luma: pendant rooms 75.6-122.6, disk rooms 137.6-197.9, a 2.62x whole-tour swing.
changelog.measured: One-variable A/B, same scene / same 3 points / 2048x1024 @ 32 spp, only the pendant wattage changed (qa-evidence/360-v2/t13/pendant-ab.json). cp-bed-2 30 W -> 75.61, 94.5 W -> 108.87, 141.7 W -> 123.73 · cp-living 30 -> 122.55, 135.4 -> 136.66, 203.1 -> 143.08 · cp-dining 30 -> 80.05, 134.6 -> 102.70, 201.9 -> 113.11. ⭐ The response SATURATES (the view transform compresses): the first tripling buys +33.3 luma at cp-bed-2, a further +50 % of power buys only +14.9. So '40 + 6 * area_m2' takes ~70 % of the achievable gain at half the wattage of the alternative tested, and a 203 W bedroom pendant was rejected as both unphysical and barely better. Residual whole-tour swing 1.93x (102.7-197.9); closing it further is an EXPOSURE/albedo question, not a wattage one — left for the board.
changelog.safety: The T07/T12 ceiling-clip bar holds: the pure-white fraction of the top 5 % of rows is 0.0000 % at all three points at both candidate wattages. The extra white pixels (0.34 % at cp-bed-2) are the lamp SHADE itself, in a 18-28 deg pitch band — a lit luminaire being the brightest thing in a room is correct, not a clip.

changelog.change: surfaces.hdri: clarens_midday (2k) -> qwantani_noon_puresky (4k); rot_z_deg 145.0 -> 38.9 (measured); the row gains exterior_class + selection_rule.
changelog.why: CONTRACT §17.2/§17.3, C-360-90 + C-360-91 (amendment A9): a V2 tour render's exterior must be NON-LOCATING, and the environment must be selected by recorded identity rather than a directory scan. clarens_midday is a photographed, nameable landscape and is classified `locating` in its provenance row; it is OUT of this lock and stays pinned only so the pre-T13 scenes remain reproducible.
changelog.not_a_redirection: This is an asset swap ordered by an architect ruling, not a rename or a change of style direction — ruling_state's 'new version file' clause governs THOSE (OQ-V2-3) and is untouched. The change is loud by construction: the style lock's sha256 is inside every render key (render_tour.mjs sceneFreshness), so it re-renders the world.

direction: warm-neutral modern: oak + oatmeal fabric + matte black metal + white ceramic, no pattern, no gloss beyond ceramic and glass
ruling_state: OQ-V2-3 DEFAULT IN PLAY — 'Habait Modern' is V2-PLAN §9's proposed default name/direction and is NOT yet Slava-ruled. A rename or a redirection is a NEW VERSION FILE (style-<slug>-v2.json / a new style_slug), never an edit of this one: root CLAUDE.md §2 makes a style change a release.

integrity.rule: every model this style locks carries the sha256 of the exact file on disk; build_scene.py re-hashes each one at build time and REFUSES to build on a mismatch (rail 4: CC0 provenance or it doesn't land).

front_axis_note: Every model here faces local -Y. For the Kenney kit that is the glTF convention (+Z-forward becomes -Y under the importer's Y-up->Z-up conversion) and it is confirmed by the six highest-confidence tall-mass measurements (bed 0.81, chair 0.94, toilet 0.56, mirror 1.00, hood 1.00, sink 0.71); the low-confidence +Y guesses on box-shaped pieces (fridge, cabinets) are the heuristic's failure mode, not a second convention. Each model's own measurement is kept beside the decision so a future eye can overrule it.

fabric_dark.use: accent upholstery, dark cushions, the door mat

art_panel.use: the print inside a picture frame — a plain warm-neutral panel, ⛔ never an image
art_panel.why: T13: the only wall-art model in the catalog (polyhaven-hanging_picture_frame_01) ships a PLACEHOLDER artwork texture reading 'Ray Hopes / Photo: 76cm x 51cm / Frame: 84cm x 59cm', legible at 1:1 in the six rooms that get art. A locked style has no licensed artwork to put there and must not invent one, so the frame gets a plain panel one step darker than the wall — it reads as a framed piece at a glance and asserts nothing.

metal_brushed.use: taps, appliance fronts, the extractor hood

glass_clear.use: appliance and shower glazing — the same shadow-ray Transparent BSDF the architectural glazing uses (T03's finding)

mirror_glass.use: the bathroom mirror pane -- a GLOSSY PALE DIELECTRIC, deliberately not a true metal mirror. Measured on this model: its pane is the back panel of a shallow niche and its normal faces the wall, so a metallic=1 mirror renders as a near-black rectangle (it reflects the 2 cm gap behind itself), and a transmissive glass renders dark for the same reason. A glossy off-white panel reads as a mirror at pano resolution and cannot go black whichever way the normal points. ⚠ Known cosmetic limitation, carried to T13.

material_map_note: ⭐ The Kenney/Quaternius models carry NAMED materials (carpet/wood/metal/…) and no image textures at all, so the style is applied by REBINDING those names to this palette — the reference's 'style is a suffix' idea, one layer down. This is what closes catalog/RESEARCH.md §8's coherence risk: the geometry stays low-poly, the material stops being a game-asset flat colour. Poly Haven rows keep their own PBR maps (material_policy: keep_source).

hdri.provenance_row: pipeline/probe/probe-assets/PROVENANCE.md (+ its pin, assets.lock.json) — NOT catalog/catalog.manifest.json, which holds the 57 furniture/texture rows only. This is T13's one-line answer to CONTRACT A9-8's open question 'which file carries the environment asset's provenance row'.
hdri.selection_rule: CONTRACT A9-7 / C-360-91: build_scene.py selects the environment BY THIS RECORDED IDENTITY (slug + sha256) and refuses on a missing file, a hash mismatch, more than one candidate for the slug, or exterior_class != 'non-locating'. ⛔ It never scans a directory and never 'picks the first one'.
hdri.rot_z_why: 38.9 deg is MEASURED, not chosen: a world-only equirect probe photographed the HDRI's own sun disc and a marker placed along the modelled SUN lamp's direction in the SAME frame, at rot 0 and rot 90 (deltas -38.855 deg and +51.164 deg, slope 1.0002/deg), so rot 38.9 puts the two suns on the same bearing. Their elevations differ by 2.3 deg (54.3 measured vs the rig's 52.0) and are left alone. ⚠ T06's inherited 145.0 for clarens_midday was never verified by this method and is ~98 deg off — it lit the pilot with two suns from different bearings for T03-T12.
hdri.resolution_why: 4k (17.9 MB). The delivered pano is 8192x4096, so this is a 2x linear undersample where clarens_midday_2k was 4x (G0's own worst-pixel finding). On a cloudless gradient sky 2x is not resolvable; 8k (71.8 MB, ~536 MB of float RGBA on a 4 GB card) buys nothing a sky this smooth can show, and the VRAM is wanted for the catalog.

floor_outdoor.use: balcony / service-balcony slabs -- a pale porcelain terrace tile, so the glazing reads as a boundary between two materials instead of one continuous oak floor

floor_wet.use: bathroom / WC slabs -- a pale large-format porcelain tile. An Israeli wet room is tiled, not laid in oak, and the draft render made that obvious the moment the bathroom had fixtures standing on it.

ceiling_luminaire.why: ⭐ THE T07 FIX. T06 hung a POINT light 15 cm under the ceiling at the room's deepest point — which is also where place_cameras.py puts the camera — so the ceiling directly above it received ~I/d^2 and clipped to pure white 255 (measured at cp-wc and cp-master-lobby, T07). A Cycles AREA light emits from its FRONT FACE only: mounted flush and facing straight down it puts NO direct light on the ceiling at all, at any position, so the clip cannot recur. The visible fixture is a separate thin disc with a mild emission, so the zenith reads as a luminaire instead of a hotspot.

pendant_bulb.energy_w_why: v1.2.0 — the ceiling luminaire's own rule, shared. A bare number is still legal (build_scene.luminaire_energy_w accepts both), so an older lock keeps building; see this file's changelog for the one-variable A/B that chose it.

daylight_panel.why: Cycles has had no light portals since 3.0; a room whose only aperture is one wide glazed opening keeps a noisy interior without a soft panel just inside it (T03). Placed only where a room's own glazing is wider than 200 cm.

sofa.note: ⚠ STYLE DECISION, made by eye on a draft render, not by rule: the catalog's other CC0 modern sofa (quaternius-X5kQPKzAWp, an L-shaped sectional) is licence-clean and correctly scaled, but at 234 x 164 cm it fills the pilot's 3.7 m living room and its low-poly cushion mass reads as one white blob at pano resolution. Kept in the catalog manifest, kept OUT of style v1. A style version that wants an L-sofa adds it back here.
